domain_label: Movie Studio — Director's Generation Feedback Loop (QC Gates, Defect-to-Lever Dispatch, Budgets, A/B Trials, Regression)
purpose: A method for the per-shot generation feedback loop a code director runs on the Higgsfield surface: four ordered QC gates (realism, identity/continuity, genre fidelity, story function), a defect-to-lever dispatch table (prompt tweak vs re-roll vs model swap vs post-fix vs shot redesign), credit-aware iteration budgets with stop rules per shot and per reel, one-variable A/B style trials with kept-result logging per the owner's try-different-keep-what-wins directive, a regression log that keeps fixed defect classes fixed, and a compression-acceptance rule for when imperfection ships versus when the shot is redesigned — every platform capability quoted from the live MCP enumeration and every artifact/physics claim carried at the honesty tag its research file gave it.
assumptions: no generation runs have happened yet: all iteration caps and budget splits are pipeline policy priors to be recalibrated once get_cost:true probes return real per-model prices, which are [UNKNOWN] on the enumerated surface

Higgsfield model ids, parameters, durations, media roles and the 1,010-credit / plus-plan account state come exclusively from the live MCP enumeration of 2026-07-03 (higgsfield_surface.md); nothing platform-side is quoted from memory

artifact-taxonomy and physics-benchmark numbers (VideoPhy 39.6%, VideoPhy-2 22%, PhysVid ~33%, Diel 55.54% human accuracy) come from research grounded largely via search excerpts and HF abstracts because the egress proxy 403-blocked primary fetches; that one-notch-down provenance is carried, not hidden

the QC rubric's noticeability ordering is an editorial synthesis the research file itself tagged [ESTIMATE] (no fetched study ranks cue noticeability directly); this KB keeps that flag rather than promoting the order to fact

the owner's stitched-reel format (3-6 s clips, 9:16, two personas, classic-luxurious genre) is taken as given by the owner brief; this KB governs how shots iterate to acceptance, not what the reel says
exclusions: prompt authoring craft itself (lighting grammar, camera-move vocabulary, transition frame-pair specs) — the cinematography and prompting specialists own writing the prompt; this KB owns deciding WHEN a prompt gets rewritten versus another lever pulled
timeline editing, grading and cover selection mechanics — the editor specialist owns Resolve-side execution; this KB only consumes the pass/fail signals those checks emit
posting cadence, Trial Reels scheduling and account analytics — media-manager scope; this KB stops at the ship/hold verdict per reel
any guidance for evoking a specific real person while hiding the face — that lane is closed and stays closed
inventing per-model credit prices, rate limits, engagement statistics or artifact base rates the grounding files marked [UNKNOWN]

competency_questions.question: What is the per-shot feedback loop's shape, and why do stills gate before any video credit is spent?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FEEDBACK_LOOP_FRAME states the generate -> gate -> classify -> dispatch-lever -> retry loop with three checkpoints (start-frame still, raw video, post-edit reel on a phone) and the stills-fail-cheap ordering, and QC_GATE_ORDER gives the fixed gate order realism -> identity/continuity -> genre -> story with earlier-gate failure voiding later gates

competency_questions.question: What exactly does the realism gate score, and what are its re-roll thresholds?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REALISM_GATE lists the 10 rubric items in noticeability order (text/logos first, skin micro-texture last), the 0/1/2 scoring, and the gates: any single 2 => re-roll, total >= 4 => re-roll, total 2-3 post-fixable only if the offending region is croppable/gradeable, carrying the ordering's [ESTIMATE] flag

competency_questions.question: How does the identity/continuity gate handle the two-persona program given the platform's Soul and Element constraints?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: IDENTITY_CONTINUITY_GATE states one soul_id per generation (so a two-persona shot cannot use two Souls), routes two-persona shots through Reference Elements placeholders, holds the Elements-vs-Souls fidelity gap [UNKNOWN], and includes skin-tone-consistency-as-identity at the grade layer plus cut-boundary vector/luminance matching

competency_questions.question: Given a named defect, how is the fixing lever chosen?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DEFECT_CLASSIFICATION separates per-seed from systematic defects and names the three taxonomy domains (temporal, structural, semantic) with the 30-type detail held [UNKNOWN], and DEFECT_LEVER_DISPATCH gives the table: per-seed => re-roll; systematic prompt-addressable => prompt tweak; systematic model-shaped => model swap; croppable cosmetic => post-fix; known-hard class => straight to shot redesign

competency_questions.question: What can a prompt tweak actually fix, and where is its hard limit?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LEVER_PROMPT_TWEAK cites physics-negative prompting's ~33% VideoPhy improvement (PhysVid), single-source lighting and logo-free styling as prompt-level fixes, one main move per shot, AND the PhyGenBench hard limit that prompt engineering is insufficient for dynamic physics — prompts reduce, never guarantee — with a two-failed-rounds escalation rule

competency_questions.question: When does the director re-roll versus swap models, and which swap constraints does the enumerated catalog impose?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LEVER_REROLL scopes re-rolls to per-seed artifacts with a 2-3-roll persistence test, and LEVER_MODEL_SWAP grounds swaps in the VideoPhy model spread and the owner's try-different directive, staying inside the enumerated catalog (seedance_2_0 for identity, kling3_0 multi-shot, wan2_7 native 2-3 s, veo3_1 start-image-only, cinematic_studio_3_0 both-frames + genre) with duration minima and per-model color-signature trim presets

competency_questions.question: What can post fix, and what is irrecoverable in post?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LEVER_POST_FIX lists crop/punch-in, reframe, grain+grade, speed ramps, whip-blur bridging and video_deflicker as post levers gated on croppable/gradeable rubric-2-3 residuals, and names the irrecoverables: clipped exposure, AI-mush texture zones, broken contact physics (the starred-row zeros)

competency_questions.question: Which shot classes are known-hard, and what does redesign look like instead of retrying them?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LEVER_SHOT_REDESIGN enumerates the eight known-hard classes (eating/drinking, dexterous hand-object work, athletic action, feet-prominent walking, legible text/badges, mirrors, crowds, held fluid pours) and the imply-rather-than-show workaround grammar

competency_questions.question: How are iteration budgets set and enforced per shot and per reel when per-model credit costs are unknown?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CREDIT_PREFLIGHT states the 1,010-credit balance, that per-generation cost is [UNKNOWN] on the surface, and that get_cost:true is the zero-spend probe run per model x resolution x duration cell before budget math; SHOT_ITERATION_BUDGET gives per-shot attempt ceilings with the accept/redesign/drop trichotomy at the ceiling; REEL_ITERATION_BUDGET gives hero-first allocation, the recut-smaller rule, and the reserved exploration share

competency_questions.question: How are A/B style trials run and their winners kept, per the owner's try-different-keep-what-wins directive?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: AB_STYLE_TRIALS mandates one variable per trial run at the cheap tier first, distinguishes native Trial Reels (whole-reel, non-follower-first, held one notch down in provenance) from cover-only iteration which is observational, and KEPT_RESULT_LOG requires the full recipe (model id, params, prompt, element/reference ids, job_id, seam type, gate scores) so every win is reproducible

competency_questions.question: How does a fixed defect class stay fixed?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REGRESSION_LOG defines the class -> fix -> recurrence-check triple, re-checks previously fixed classes on their trigger shots each batch, and reopens affected classes when the model catalog changes

competency_questions.question: When is imperfection accepted because compression will hide it, and when must the shot be redesigned instead — and how does the reel finally ship?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMPRESSION_ACCEPTANCE states compression launders low-level cues (frequency fingerprints, micro-texture, faint boiling) but never semantic/geometric tells (garbled logos, finger counts, foot slide, shadow direction, identity drift, object counts), with acceptance decided on a phone at feed resolution; SHIP_DECISION composes gates, budget ledger, kept-result and regression checks into the go/hold verdict

competency_questions.question: Why can an automated VLM critic not be the only QC gate?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: AUTOMATED_CRITIC_LIMITS cites Artifact-Bench's finding that 19 leading MLLMs were near or below random in challenging artifact-spotting settings and misaligned with human perception, positions the surface's video_analysis_* tools as pre-filters, and requires a human verdict on starred rubric rows

competency_questions.question: What do the genre-fidelity and story-function gates each check, and why do they run after realism and identity?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GENRE_FIDELITY_GATE checks the classic-luxurious read (muted rolled-off highlights, warm-neutral palette, motivated lighting only, one main camera move); STORY_FUNCTION_GATE checks the shot's reel job — seam frame-pair constraints, first-3-seconds hook placement, Murch emotion-first — and both are stated as adjustable-by-prompt-or-post, which is why they rank after the irrecoverable-failure gates

glossary.definition: One of four ordered pass/fail checks every generated asset must clear before the next is run: realism (artifact rubric), identity/continuity (persona and cut-boundary match), genre fidelity (classic-luxurious read), story function (the shot's job in the reel). Failing an earlier gate voids the later ones — nothing downstream is polished on an asset that will be regenerated.

A realism-rubric item scored 2 = visible at a glance. Per the research file's gate: any single 2 forces a re-roll; rubric total >= 4 forces a re-roll; totals of 2-3 may go to post only if the offending region is croppable or gradeable [ESTIMATE-ordered rubric carried from realism_antiai.md §5].

The named category a failure is filed under before a lever is chosen — top-level domains per Artifact-Bench: temporal inconsistencies, structural distortions, semantic incoherence [FACT — abstract via HF paper_search; the 30 fine-grained type labels sit in the proxy-blocked paper body, [UNKNOWN]]. The class plus its persistence (per-seed vs systematic) determines the lever.

One of five escalating responses to a failed gate: prompt tweak, re-roll, model swap, post-fix, shot redesign. Dispatch is cheapest-first with two exceptions: known-hard shot classes skip straight to redesign, and starred-row zeros can never route to post-fix.

Regenerating with the same prompt/model to exploit stochastic variation; the cheapest fix for per-seed artifacts (one bad hand, one flicker burst). A defect that survives 2-3 rolls is reclassified systematic and escalates — more rolls of the same dice are sunk cost.

The sanctioned zero-spend price probe: get_cost:true on a generate_* call returns the credit cost WITHOUT submitting [FACT — generate_* schemas, live MCP surface 2026-07-03]. Because per-model credit prices are [UNKNOWN] on the enumerated surface, every model x resolution x duration cell must be preflighted before budget math.

Running counts of rubric-class failures per model x shot-type, built from every gate result. It is what turns the owner's try-different directive into routing: the dispatch table consults it before choosing a swap target.

The record of every winner: model id, full params (resolution/duration/genre/cfg/speedramp), prompt text, element/reference ids, job_id, seam type, gate scores. A win whose recipe was not captured is not a win — it cannot be reproduced or reused.

The fixed-defect registry: defect class -> the fix that killed it (prompt clause, model choice, design rule) -> the check that would catch recurrence. Each batch re-runs the checks for previously fixed classes; a model-catalog change reopens the affected classes.

A shot class documented as failing current video models regardless of iteration: eating/drinking to the mouth, dexterous hand-object manipulation, athletic full-body action, feet-prominent walking, legible text/badge close-ups, mirrors showing the subject, crowds, held hero fluid pours [FACT/ESTIMATE mix carried per realism_antiai.md §6]. These dispatch directly to shot redesign.

The deliberate decision to ship a low-level residual because platform recompression and a ~6-inch phone screen will hide it. Legal only for laundered cues (micro-texture waxiness, faint boiling, missing grain); never for semantic/geometric tells (logos, fingers, foot slide, shadows, identity, counts), which survive any bitrate.

nodes.definition: Frame the director's core work unit: for every shot, run generate -> gate -> classify -> dispatch-lever -> retry until accepted or stopped. Three QC checkpoints anchor the loop [carried from realism_antiai.md §5]: the start/end keyframe stills (rubric items text, identity, permanence, shadows, background, skin), the raw video (all items), and the post-edit reel at final resolution on an actual phone. The loop is stills-first because failing cheap is the design: the reel is planned as a chain of stills, and a keyframe pair that fails any gate is regenerated BEFORE video generation — stills are cheaper than video as a category [FACT — cost-ordering claim in editing_grading_poster.md §6; exact Higgsfield prices [UNKNOWN] until get_cost preflight]. The loop is worst-artifact-driven, not average-quality-driven: an Instagram follower sees dozens of clips, and one blatant tell (garbled logo, six fingers, sliding feet) flips the account's perceived authenticity permanently [ESTIMATE — operational reading of the detection studies, carried from realism_antiai.md §3].

included: the generate->gate->classify->dispatch->retry loop shape
three checkpoints: keyframe stills, raw video, post-edit reel on a phone
stills-fail-cheap ordering and worst-artifact-driven QC
excluded: what the gates check (their own nodes)
how prompts are authored (cinematography/prompting specialists)

pros.claim: Gating keyframe stills before video generation converts image-QC wins into video wins at the cheapest point of failure
pros.example: rejecting a start frame with a garbled hotel sign at the still stage instead of discovering it inside a rendered 6 s clip

cons.claim: A per-shot loop with three checkpoints adds latency per shot versus batch-generating a whole reel and triaging afterward
cons.example: a 7-shot reel serialized through still-QC before any video runs, versus one parallel batch that wastes credits on doomed shots

failure_modes: animating a keyframe pair that never passed still-stage gates
judging shots by average quality and shipping one glaring worst-artifact tell
acceptance_tests: the analysis states the loop shape, the three checkpoints including phone-screen final QC, the stills-first cost ordering with the exact-prices-[UNKNOWN] caveat, and the worst-artifact-driven principle
revisit_triggers: get_cost probes show still-vs-video cost ratios that change the fail-cheap ordering
a batch workflow proves faster without raising waste
a fourth checkpoint (e.g. post-upload re-check) becomes necessary

base.update_signal: real per-model prices or observed batch economics change the loop's cost ordering

nodes.definition: Fix the gate order the owner asked for: (1) realism, (2) identity/continuity, (3) genre fidelity, (4) story function. The order is severity-and-recoverability logic: realism failures are the owner's #1 requirement and largely irrecoverable in post (the starred rubric rows — clipped exposure, AI-mush texture, broken physics — force regeneration [carried from editing_grading_poster.md §5]); identity drift threatens the whole two-persona program and compounds across shots; genre and story are the most adjustable gates — a grade or a recut can move them without regenerating pixels. Honesty carried: no fetched study ranks cue noticeability directly, so the within-realism ordering is the research file's editorial synthesis [ESTIMATE — moderate-high confidence, realism_antiai.md §5]. Rule: failing an earlier gate voids later gates — never grade, seam-match, or story-judge an asset that will be regenerated.

included: the fixed four-gate order and its recoverability rationale
earlier-failure-voids-later-gates rule
the [ESTIMATE] flag on noticeability ordering
excluded: each gate's internal checklist (their own nodes)
the levers a failure dispatches to (dispatch node)

pros.claim: Ordering gates by irrecoverability means QC effort lands where post cannot save the shot
pros.example: catching foot-slide (regenerate-only) before spending grading time on a clip that gets thrown away

cons.claim: A strict serial order can hide multi-gate information — a shot failing realism is discarded before its genre drift is even noticed and logged
cons.example: five consecutive re-rolls all secretly too teal, discovered only after realism finally passes

failure_modes: polishing genre/story on a shot with an open realism defect
treating the noticeability ordering as fetched fact rather than the flagged editorial synthesis
acceptance_tests: the analysis states the four gates in order with the recoverability rationale, the voiding rule, and the [ESTIMATE] status of the noticeability ordering

nodes.definition: Gate 1: score the shot on the 10-item rubric ordered by human noticeability [ESTIMATE-ordered, carried]: (1) text/logos/badges, (2) hands in motion, (3) contact physics (foot slide, wheel slip, hover, splash-from-nothing), (4) identity lock vs reference sheet, (5) object permanence and count, (6) shadow/reflection geometry, (7) motion quality (Newtonian accelerations, cloth/hair inertia), (8) texture stability (boiling, edge shimmer), (9) background coherence, (10) skin micro-texture. Each 0 = clean, 1 = visible on inspection, 2 = visible at a glance. Gate: any single 2 => re-roll; total >= 4 => re-roll; total 2-3 => post-fixable only if the offending region is croppable/gradeable [carried from realism_antiai.md §5]. Why motion items rank high: physics is where models objectively fail — best VideoPhy model passed caption+physics in only 39.6% of instances, VideoPhy-2 hard subset 22%, and conservation laws are the named worst area [FACT — abstracts via HF paper_search]. Static faces are a mostly-won battle (AI faces judged human 69.5% vs 52.2% for real in the hyperrealism study [FACT — via search excerpt]) — do not overspend QC there.

included: the 10 ordered items with 0/1/2 scoring
the re-roll thresholds and the croppable/gradeable post condition
the physics-benchmark grounding for motion-first attention
excluded: which lever fixes a given failure (dispatch node)
identity detail beyond rubric item 4 (identity gate)

pros.claim: A numeric per-item rubric with hard thresholds makes the realism verdict repeatable across shots and reviewers instead of vibes-based
pros.example: two different QC passes both re-rolling a clip because the wheel-slip item scored 2, regardless of how good the lighting looked

cons.claim: The rubric's ordering and thresholds are editorial priors, so early batches may over- or under-reject until calibrated
cons.example: the total>=4 threshold rejecting compression-safe clips whose four 1-scores were all in low-priority texture items

failure_modes: averaging away a single glaring 2 because the rest of the shot is clean
spending QC attention on skin micro-texture while a contact-physics item goes unchecked
acceptance_tests: the analysis lists all 10 items in order, the 0/1/2 scale, both re-roll thresholds, the croppable/gradeable condition, and cites the 39.6%/22% physics pass rates for motion-first priority

base.update_signal: threshold calibration data or the full Artifact-Bench taxonomy changes the rubric

nodes.definition: Gate 2: verify the persona and the seams. Identity: face geometry, eye color, hair, wardrobe identical to the reference sheet within-shot and across shots — identity drift is a named industry failure mode [FACT — via search excerpts, realism_antiai.md §2a]. Platform constraints bind the check [FACT — live MCP surface]: a trained Soul is usable only with soul_2/soul_cinematic and ONE soul_id per generation, so a two-persona shot cannot use two Souls — two-person shots route through Reference Elements (<<<element_id>>> placeholders, multiple allowed per prompt); whether Elements degrade identity fidelity versus Souls is [UNKNOWN — only testable by generation]. Continuity: both personas' skin tones must land on the same target values across every clip — skin consistency IS character consistency at the grade layer [carried from editing_grading_poster.md §3.3]; at each cut boundary the dominant motion vector, subject screen-position, and boundary-frame luminance/hue must match the seam plan. A shot that passes realism but drifts identity still fails — the gate runs even on artifact-clean assets.

included: identity match to the reference sheet within and across shots
the one-soul_id and Elements-for-two-persona routing constraints
skin-tone and cut-boundary vector/luminance continuity checks
excluded: training Souls / creating Elements (character specialist)
the grading mechanics that fix a mismatch (editor specialist)

pros.claim: Checking identity against a fixed reference sheet catches drift that per-shot realism scoring is blind to
pros.example: clip 4's jacket buttons and eye color quietly differing from clips 1-3, caught only by sheet comparison, not by any artifact score

cons.claim: The Elements route required for two-persona shots carries an unmeasured fidelity gap versus Souls, so the gate may pass assets whose identity hold is weaker than solo shots
cons.example: a two-persona dinner shot holding wardrobe but softening the male persona's face geometry relative to his Soul-generated solos

failure_modes: attempting two Souls in one generation (surface-impossible) instead of routing via Elements
letting each clip's skin land on different grade values so the persona reads as different people

nodes.definition: Gate 3: does the shot read classic-luxurious, not gauche or generic-AI-slick? Checklist from the grounded craft files: muted, rolled-off highlights rather than clipped whites — flagged as the strongest single 'expensive film' cue [ESTIMATE — colorist craft, editing_grading_poster.md §3.2]; warm-neutral old-money palette (cream, beige, camel, navy, sage), global chroma restrained, nothing neon [FACT/excerpt — style guides]; motivated lighting only — every light justifiable by an in-world source, since unmotivated glow is a recognized CG/AI tell [FACT on the definition; the AI-tell linkage ESTIMATE, cinematography file §1.1]; one main camera move per shot with a speed modifier — multi-move prompts degrade coherence [FACT-1src — Kling guidance]; one small living micro-detail per shot (steam, curtain, hair) for the quiet-luxury read. Fitness-accent posts may push contrast/saturation slightly but stay inside the palette family so the grid stays coherent. Genre failures are usually prompt- or grade-adjustable, which is exactly why this gate ranks third.

the fitness-accent tolerance band
why genre ranks third (adjustability)
excluded: authoring the lighting/lens prompt language (cinematography specialist)

pros.claim: A concrete genre checklist stops style drift across batches that per-shot realism QC would never flag
pros.example: rejecting a technically clean clip whose clipped windows and neon-teal shadows read blockbuster-cheap against the old-money grid

cons.claim: Genre judgment is the most taste-laden gate, and over-enforcing restraint can flatten the pattern interrupts short-form retention needs
cons.example: muting a hook shot so thoroughly it loses the first-3-seconds pop that keeps viewers past the drop-off cliff

nodes.definition: Gate 4: the shot must do its job in the reel, judged against the reel plan. Seam duty: the shot list is really a transition list — clip N's end frame and clip N+1's start frame must satisfy the chosen seam's constraints (matched shape/screen-position for a match cut, matched vector and blur for a whip bridge, full occlusion for a masked wipe) [FACT/excerpt-grounded transition table, cinematography file §3]. Hook duty: up to ~50% of viewers drop off within the first 3 seconds [FACT/excerpt], so the strongest image goes first with a pattern interrupt inside clip 1 — a hook shot that merely looks good but poses no visual question fails this gate. Rhythm duty: Murch's Rule of Six puts emotion first (51%) and says sacrifice from the bottom [FACT/excerpt]; eye-trace across 3 s shots means the next shot's subject sits where the previous shot left the viewer's eye. A beautiful clip that breaks its seam pair or dulls the hook fails gate 4 even with gates 1-3 clean; the fix is usually a keyframe re-spec or a reel-plan edit, not a full regeneration.

hook placement against the 3-second drop-off
Murch emotion-first and eye-trace duties
excluded: choosing the transitions themselves (cinematography file)

pros.claim: Judging shots against their reel job prevents a gallery of pretty clips that cut together badly
pros.example: failing a gorgeous orbit clip because its end frame exits screen-left while the next clip's whip enters screen-right, breaking the seam vector

cons.claim: Story judgment depends on a reel plan that may itself be wrong, so gate 4 can enforce conformance to a weak plan
cons.example: rejecting a stronger spontaneous hook because the plan called for a different opening image

nodes.definition: Bound what automation may decide. Artifact-Bench evaluated 19 leading multimodal LLMs on artifact spotting: many were near or below random in challenging settings, and MLLM judgments significantly misalign with human perceptual preference [FACT — abstract via HF paper_search]. Consequence: the surface's video_analysis_create/status/jobs tools and any VLM rubric-scorer are useful PRE-FILTERS — cheap triage that can auto-reject obvious failures and rank candidates — but cannot be the only gate; a human verdict is required on the starred rubric rows (text/logos, contact physics, texture mush, exposure) before a shot is accepted. Second calibration fact: human confidence is itself miscalibrated — the most-confident judges made the most errors in the hyperrealism study (Dunning-Kruger pattern) [FACT — via search excerpts] — so comment-section 'this is AI' accusations will occur even on clean content; the defense is consistency across many posts, not any single perfect clip, which is exactly why the regression log exists.

human-verdict requirement on starred rows
the miscalibrated-audience corollary
excluded: building the VLM critic prompt itself (prompting specialist)

pros.example: video_analysis auto-rejecting 6 of 10 candidates for obvious flicker, a human then applying starred-row judgment to the surviving 4

cons.claim: Keeping a human on every starred-row verdict caps loop throughput and adds a subjective bottleneck automation was meant to remove
cons.example: a 40-shot week where every candidate clip awaits one person's phone-screen check

failure_modes: letting a VLM score be the sole accept signal on starred rows
treating audience accusations as ground truth instead of tracking the rubric
acceptance_tests: the analysis cites the 19-MLLM near-random finding, positions video_analysis_* as pre-filter, requires human verdicts on starred rows, and carries the audience-miscalibration corollary

nodes.definition: Classify before fixing. Every gate failure is filed as (defect class, persistence). nodes.definition: Lever 2 — the cheapest fix for per-seed artifacts. nodes.definition: The accept-imperfection rule. Platforms recompress aggressively, and the forensics literature is explicit that this launders low-level cues: block effects obscure artifacts, textural information is lost, detectors degrade on platform-compressed video [FACT — via search excerpts of compressed-deepfake papers]. Therefore compression HIDES: generator frequency fingerprints and upsampling signatures [FACT — the named low-level cues], skin micro-texture waxiness, faint boiling/shimmer, film-grain absence [ESTIMATE — high-frequency phenomena of the kind compression removes, high confidence]; a ~6-inch 9:16 phone screen shrinks fine detail further [ESTIMATE; quantified small-screen detection deltas [UNKNOWN]]. Compression does NOT hide semantic/geometric tells: garbled logos, wrong finger counts, foot sliding, shadow-direction errors, identity drift, object-count changes — these survive any bitrate and are the cues human raters use anyway [ESTIMATE — reasoned from what DCT-style compression removes vs preserves, high confidence]. Acceptance rule: only residuals in rubric items 8-10 territory (texture stability, background fine detail, skin micro-texture) may be accepted, and only after the shot passes final QC on an actual phone at feed resolution; items 1-6 are never acceptance candidates — their lever is regeneration or redesign. Honest flip side: compression also ADDS blockiness that can make borderline texture worse [ESTIMATE — moderate], so acceptance is verified on the compressed artifact, not predicted from the master.

the individual checks' mechanics (their own nodes)

pros.claim: A composed checklist verdict prevents shipping on partial evidence — strong clips cannot outvote one open tell
pros.example: holding an otherwise excellent reel because the regression check found the signage clause dropped from shot 2's prompt

cons.claim: A strict all-conditions verdict can starve posting cadence while shots iterate
cons.example: a week without a publish because two seams keep missing their luminance window

failure_modes: shipping with an unverified compression acceptance
holding without naming the failing node so the retry re-enters the loop classless
acceptance_tests: the analysis lists every GO condition, requires named-node HOLDs, and states the worst-artifact-driven single-tell hold rule
revisit_triggers: cadence pressure forces a tiered verdict (e.g. story-lite posts)
a shipped reel surfaces a tell the verdict missed
the owner changes the risk tolerance

base.update_signal: a missed tell in a shipped reel or a cadence policy change re-weights the verdict

edges.why_related: the gate order sequences the checks inside the loop the frame defines
the loop's fail-cheap ordering only becomes quantitative once the preflight prices each attempt
realism is gate 1 in the fixed order and inherits the voiding rule
identity/continuity is gate 2 and runs only on realism-clean assets
genre is gate 3, placed by the adjustability rationale the order node states
story function is gate 4, the last check before dispatch or acceptance
the critic-limits boundary is defined over the realism rubric's starred rows
rubric rows that fire are the raw material classification files into classes
identity and continuity failures enter the same class-and-persistence filing as realism failures
only a defect classified systematic-and-prompt-addressable routes to a prompt rewrite
the per-seed classification is the precondition for spending a re-roll
re-roll caps are denominated in probed credit prices, not attempt counts
a model-shaped systematic classification is what justifies swapping generators
swap candidates are compared on probed per-cell prices, since per-model cost is [UNKNOWN] until probed
post-fix eligibility (croppable/gradeable residual at rubric 2-3) is a classification outcome
matching a defect to a known-hard class is the classification act that triggers straight redesign
the dispatch table's prompt row encodes this lever's scope and two-round limit
the dispatch table's per-seed row encodes the re-roll lever and its reclassification exit
the dispatch table's model-shaped row consumes the swap lever and its catalog constraints
the dispatch table's cosmetic-residual row consumes the post lever and its irrecoverable ban
the dispatch table's known-hard skip and escalation terminus both land on redesign
the budget ceiling counts and prices the attempts dispatch keeps issuing
reel allocation sums and ranks the per-shot ceilings across the shot list
model choice is the primary trial axis, and trials inherit the swap node's catalog constraints
a trial only counts when its winner enters the log with a full recipe
the regression registry's fixes reference logged recipes (the prompt clause or model that killed a class)
regression entries are keyed by the same defect classes classification defines
the acceptance lane is defined over the rubric's items 8-10 versus the never-hidden items 1-6
the ship verdict requires every shot's story-function pass including seam frame-pair conformance
the verdict requires the budget ledger closed within the envelope or a recut
green recurrence checks for the batch are a GO condition
every accepted imperfection in the verdict must carry this node's phone-verified acceptance
per-attempt cheapness pulls toward one more roll while the ceiling exists precisely to stop that pull
edges.resolution_rule: the ceiling wins unconditionally: at the cap the accept/redesign/drop trichotomy fires and no further rolls are granted on sunk-cost grounds; below the cap, re-roll remains the cheapest first lever for per-seed defects

edges.why_related: the acceptance lane forgives residuals the rubric scored, so it pressures the gate's strictness
edges.resolution_rule: the split resolves by cue physics: only items 8-10 low-level residuals may be accepted after phone-screen verification; items 1-6 semantic/geometric tells survive compression and the realism gate's re-roll verdict stands

edges.why_related: exploration spend competes with finishing the current reel inside its envelope
edges.resolution_rule: the reserved exploration share resolves it structurally: trials may not exceed the share, and the share may not be raided for exploitation — both caps hold unless the owner resizes the split

edges.why_related: prompt optimism says rewrite again; the known-hard list says the class will not yield to wording
edges.resolution_rule: the known-hard list wins: classes on it skip prompting entirely (PhyGenBench: prompt engineering insufficient for dynamic physics); off-list classes get at most two prompt rounds before escalation

edges.why_related: trial winners are picked by gate scores, so the human-verdict requirement on starred rows constrains how trial results may be judged at scale
both are regeneration levers differing only in what varies — the seed versus the generator — which is why persistence classification is what separates their use
recurrence checks feed back into the gates as standing per-class checks, tightening future QC with what past failures taught
accumulated win/failure records causally reshape the dispatch table's per-class lever choices over time

conflict_axes.name: cheap_reroll_vs_credit_ceiling
conflict_axes.description: Each re-roll is the cheapest single attempt, but unbounded rolling is the loop's classic budget sink; the ceiling exists to end iteration on schedule rather than on hope.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: ceilings are pre-committed and credit-denominated after preflight; at the cap the accept/redesign/drop trichotomy is mandatory

conflict_axes.name: compression_forgiveness_vs_zero_tolerance
conflict_axes.description: Platform recompression genuinely hides low-level cues, which tempts relaxing QC, but semantic/geometric tells survive any bitrate and one shipped tell can permanently flip perceived authenticity.
poles: accept what the feed will hide
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: split by cue physics: items 8-10 residuals may be accepted after phone-screen verification; items 1-6 never

conflict_axes.name: exploration_vs_exploitation
conflict_axes.description: The owner's try-different directive demands ongoing style trials while reel deadlines and the credit envelope pull all spend toward finishing known-good recipes.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: a reserved exploration share of each reel envelope funds trials; neither side may raid the other's allocation

conflict_axes.name: prompt_optimism_vs_known_hard_redesign
conflict_axes.description: Prompt tweaks measurably reduce some defect classes (~33% VideoPhy gain from negative physics prompting) but benchmarks show dynamic physics does not yield to wording, making repeated rewrites of known-hard shots predicted waste.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: known-hard classes skip prompting entirely; other classes get two rounds, then escalate

conflict_axes.name: automation_throughput_vs_human_judgment
conflict_axes.description: A VLM critic scales QC across batches, but Artifact-Bench shows leading MLLMs near or below random on hard artifact spotting and misaligned with human perception.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: critic as pre-filter that rejects and ranks; human verdict mandatory on starred rubric rows before accept

conflict_axes.name: per_shot_perfection_vs_reel_throughput
conflict_axes.description: Worst-artifact-driven QC holds whole reels for single tells while posting cadence and account growth want reels out the door.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: hold only on items 1-6 tells and starred-row zeros; recut the reel smaller rather than shipping a tell or overspending to perfect it

conflict_axes.name: identity_lock_vs_style_variation
conflict_axes.description: A/B style trials push toward varied looks while the two-persona program demands the personas and grade family stay recognizably constant across every post.
poles: vary the style to find winners
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: trials vary one non-identity variable at a time; persona reference sheets and skin-tone targets are never trial variables

conflict_axes.name: sunk_cost_vs_stop_rule
conflict_axes.description: Every failed attempt increases the felt pressure to continue ('the last roll was so close'), which is exactly the bias the pre-committed ceilings and trichotomy exist to defeat.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: stop rules are set before iteration begins and applied mechanically; 'almost there' is not an input to the trichotomy

conflict_axes.name: genre_restraint_vs_hook_retention
conflict_axes.description: The classic-luxurious grammar wants muted restraint while the first-3-seconds drop-off cliff rewards loud pattern interrupts.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the hook shot gets the reel's strongest image and motion inside the house palette — pattern interrupt through content and cut, not through breaking the grade

edge_cases.description: Budget math is attempted before any get_cost probe, on assumed per-model prices that the surface never published
edge_cases.trigger: a reel plan assigns credit ceilings while per-model cost is still [UNKNOWN]
edge_cases.mitigation: block budget-setting until every planned model x resolution x duration cell is preflighted with get_cost:true; until then only attempt-count priors may be used and must be flagged as such

edge_cases.description: A shot passes the whole realism rubric but the persona's eye color and jacket differ subtly from the reference sheet
edge_cases.trigger: artifact-clean generation with identity drift across shots
edge_cases.mitigation: run gate 2 against the reference sheet on every asset regardless of gate-1 score; identity is checked by comparison, not by artifact detection

edge_cases.description: A two-persona dinner shot is planned with both trained Souls, which the surface cannot execute
edge_cases.trigger: shot design assumes two soul_ids in one generation, but the surface allows only one
edge_cases.mitigation: route all two-persona shots through Reference Elements placeholders at design time, and carry the [UNKNOWN] Elements-vs-Souls fidelity gap as an explicit QC watch item

edge_cases.description: Seven re-rolls chase a clean champagne pour that the known-hard list said to redesign at roll zero
edge_cases.trigger: a known-hard defect class enters the re-roll lane instead of straight-dispatching to redesign
edge_cases.mitigation: check every new defect against the known-hard list before any lever is pulled; list members skip to redesign with zero rolls

edge_cases.description: A model swap fixes the physics defect but the new model's color signature breaks grade continuity with the reel's other clips
edge_cases.trigger: swap executed without the per-model trim step before hero-grade matching
edge_cases.mitigation: apply the per-model trim preset on first batches from any new model, then hero-match; log the signature so future swaps price this cost in

edge_cases.description: The VLM pre-filter passes a clip whose foot slide any human viewer would catch
edge_cases.trigger: automation is trusted as the final gate on a starred row
edge_cases.mitigation: require the human verdict on starred rows before accept; treat VLM passes as rank-ordering only, never as acceptance

edge_cases.description: A defect class fixed last month reappears after the model catalog silently changes
edge_cases.trigger: a platform-side model update invalidates a model-relative fix while the regression class stays marked closed
edge_cases.mitigation: re-enumerate the catalog periodically; any model change reopens the classes whose fixes depended on it and re-runs their recurrence checks

edge_cases.description: A clip carries both waxy skin (compression-hidden) and a slightly garbled marque badge (never hidden), and the acceptance lane is invoked for both
edge_cases.trigger: acceptance creep extends the items-8-10 lane to a semantic tell
edge_cases.mitigation: acceptance is evaluated per-cue, not per-clip: the waxy skin may be accepted after phone verification, the badge forces regeneration or logo-free redesign regardless

edge_cases.description: An A/B winner is kept but its cfg_scale and element ids were never logged, so the win cannot be reproduced next reel
edge_cases.trigger: keep-what-wins executed without the full recipe capture
edge_cases.mitigation: make recipe completeness a keep-blocker: a result without model id, params, prompt, reference ids and job_id cannot be marked kept

edge_cases.description: A 3-second slot is assigned to seedance1_5 (min 4 s) and the surface silently clamps the duration, breaking the reel's beat grid
edge_cases.trigger: duration minima ignored at dispatch; unsupported durations clamp to nearest allowed
edge_cases.mitigation: validate duration support per model at swap time (wan2_7 is the only 2-3 s native model); re-plan the slot or the model before generating

edge_cases.description: The reel envelope exhausts with two connective shots unshipped and pressure mounts to overspend into next reel's budget
edge_cases.trigger: budget exhaustion mid-reel with an incomplete shot list
edge_cases.mitigation: recut the reel smaller (a complete short reel with high retention beats a longer weak one) and return the concept's missing beats to the backlog

edge_cases.description: A Trial Reels run is read as a cover A/B result when the mechanism tested the entire reel against non-followers
edge_cases.trigger: misattributing whole-reel trial outcomes to a single cover variable
edge_cases.mitigation: log Trial Reels outcomes as whole-reel evidence; cover conclusions require the observational one-variable comparison across similar posts

workflow.action: Preflight the reel's cost cells and set the budget ledger
workflow.description: Run get_cost:true for every planned model x resolution x duration cell, record prices against the 1,010-credit balance, and denominate shot/reel ceilings in credits
workflow.artifact: priced budget ledger with per-shot and per-reel ceilings
workflow.gate: every planned cell has a probed price; no ceiling rests on an assumed cost

workflow.action: Generate and gate the keyframe stills before any video spend
workflow.description: Produce each seam's start/end frame pair and run the still-stage checks (text, identity, permanence, shadows, background, skin) so failures die cheap
workflow.gate: no video generation is queued for a shot whose keyframe pair has an open gate failure

workflow.action: Score the raw clip on the realism rubric
workflow.description: Apply the 10-item 0/1/2 rubric in noticeability order and compute the verdict against the any-2 and total>=4 thresholds
workflow.gate: verdict recorded: pass, post-fixable 2-3, or re-roll with the firing rows named

workflow.action: Verify identity and continuity against the reference sheet and seam plan
workflow.description: Compare persona face/wardrobe to the sheet, check skin-tone targets, and match cut-boundary vectors and luminance to the planned transition
workflow.gate: no drift versus the sheet and both boundary frames inside the seam window

workflow.action: Check the genre read and the shot's story function
workflow.description: Confirm muted highlights, house palette, motivated light and one main move; then confirm the shot does its reel job (seam pair, hook placement, eye-trace)
workflow.gate: gates 3 and 4 pass or the failure routes to prompt/grade/plan adjustment, not regeneration

workflow.action: Classify every failure by class and persistence
workflow.description: File each failed check as (domain, rubric row, per-seed vs systematic) using count<=4 siblings as the persistence test, and write it to the per-model ledger
workflow.artifact: classified defect entries in the ledger
workflow.gate: no lever is pulled on an unclassified defect

workflow.action: Dispatch the lever from the decision table
workflow.description: Route per-seed to re-roll, prompt-addressable to a max-two-round rewrite, model-shaped to a ledger-chosen swap, cosmetic residuals to post, and known-hard classes straight to redesign
workflow.artifact: dispatch decision with lever, rationale and expected cost
workflow.gate: known-hard skip and starred-row post-ban exceptions verified before execution

workflow.action: Iterate inside the shot ceiling and stop on schedule
workflow.description: Execute the dispatched lever, decrement the shot's credit ceiling, and at the cap run the mandatory accept/redesign/drop trichotomy
workflow.artifact: attempt log with running spend per shot
workflow.gate: no attempt exceeds the ceiling; every capped shot exits via the trichotomy

workflow.action: Run the reel's A/B trials from the exploration share and keep winners with full recipes
workflow.description: Vary one variable per trial at the cheap tier, judge with gate scores plus human starred-row verdicts, and log winners (model, params, prompt, ids, job_id, seam, scores)
workflow.artifact: trial results appended to the kept-result log
workflow.gate: every kept winner's recipe is complete; unattributable multi-variable wins are rejected

workflow.action: Re-run regression checks for previously fixed classes
workflow.description: Execute each registered recurrence check on its trigger shots for this batch and reopen classes affected by any catalog change
workflow.artifact: green/red regression report for the batch
workflow.gate: all recurrence checks green or the recurrences are back in dispatch with classes named

workflow.action: Make compression-acceptance calls on a phone at feed resolution
workflow.description: For rubric items 8-10 residuals only, verify invisibility on the compressed artifact on an actual phone; refuse the lane to any items 1-6 tell
workflow.gate: every acceptance is phone-verified and cue-scoped; none covers a semantic/geometric tell

workflow.description: Compose gates, seams, budget closure, recipe logging, regression greens and human sign-offs into GO, or a HOLD that names the failing node
workflow.gate: GO only with all conditions met; every HOLD carries the failing node so the retry enters dispatch classified

dominance_rules.rule: A starred-row zero dominates any post-fix ambition
dominance_rules.rationale: clipped exposure, AI-mush texture and broken contact physics are irrecoverable in the timeline; grading them wastes editor hours and still ships a tell
dominance_rules.trigger: a post-fix is proposed for a starred-row zero
dominance_rules.action: route to regeneration or redesign; post-fix is only legal for croppable/gradeable rubric 2-3 residuals

dominance_rules.rule: The known-hard list dominates lever escalation order
dominance_rules.rationale: benchmarks and documented failures predict these classes lose regardless of rolls or wording, so cheapest-first escalation is predicted waste on them
dominance_rules.trigger: a defect maps to one of the eight known-hard classes
dominance_rules.action: skip prompt and re-roll entirely and dispatch straight to shot redesign with the imply-rather-than-show grammar

dominance_rules.rationale: garbled logos, finger counts, foot slide, shadow errors, identity drift and object counts survive any bitrate and are what human raters key on
dominance_rules.trigger: an items 1-6 tell is nominated for the acceptance lane
dominance_rules.action: refuse acceptance; the only levers are regeneration or redesign, however good the rest of the clip is

dominance_rules.rule: Identity lock dominates style novelty in trials
dominance_rules.rationale: the two-persona program's value is cumulative recognizability; a style win that moves the persona or grade family is a net loss
dominance_rules.trigger: an A/B trial proposes varying a persona reference, skin-tone target, or the house grade family
dominance_rules.action: exclude identity variables from trials; style trials vary model, genre param, lighting or grade variant only, within the house family

dominance_rules.rule: The pre-committed stop rule dominates sunk cost
dominance_rules.rationale: 'almost there' is the exact bias ceilings exist to defeat; iteration that ends on hope instead of schedule drains the shared credit pool
dominance_rules.trigger: the shot ceiling is reached with pressure for one more attempt
dominance_rules.action: fire the accept/redesign/drop trichotomy mechanically; further attempts require the owner explicitly raising the ceiling, not the loop bending it

dominance_rules.rationale: per-model credit prices are [UNKNOWN] on the enumerated surface, and budget math on invented prices is fabrication
dominance_rules.trigger: any budget, cap or swap comparison is about to use an unprobed price
dominance_rules.action: run get_cost:true for the cell first; until probed, only flagged attempt-count priors may be used

dominance_rules.rule: The human verdict dominates the VLM critic on starred rows
dominance_rules.rationale: Artifact-Bench shows leading MLLMs near or below random on hard artifact spotting and misaligned with human perception
dominance_rules.trigger: an accept decision on a starred row rests only on an automated score
dominance_rules.action: hold the accept until a human applies the starred-row check, using the critic only as pre-filter and ranker

dominance_rules.rationale: keyframe defects propagate into every video attempt built on them, and stills fail at a fraction of video cost
dominance_rules.trigger: video generation is queued for a shot whose keyframe pair has an open failure
dominance_rules.action: block the video call until the still passes all applicable gates; fix the frame, not the clip

dominance_rules.rationale: an unattributable win cannot enter the kept-result log or improve dispatch, so a fast multi-variable trial produces zero reusable knowledge
dominance_rules.trigger: a trial design varies more than one variable to save time
dominance_rules.action: split it into sequential one-variable trials or drop it; the exploration share funds attribution, not anecdotes

anti_rework_rules.rule: Gate keyframe stills through all applicable checks before any video generation
anti_rework_rules.prevents: paying video-tier credits to discover a garbled sign, identity miss, or shadow error that a still-stage check would have caught for a fraction of the cost

anti_rework_rules.rule: Preflight get_cost for every planned cell before the first batch of a reel
anti_rework_rules.prevents: mid-reel budget collapse when an unprobed model turns out to cost multiples of the assumed price, forcing an unplanned recut

anti_rework_rules.rule: Classify persistence (per-seed vs systematic) with count<=4 siblings before choosing a lever
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-roll spirals on systematic defects and premature model swaps on seed luck — both classic double-spends

anti_rework_rules.rule: Check the known-hard list at shot-design time, not at QC time
anti_rework_rules.prevents: authoring, generating and failing shots (champagne pours, eating, mirror selfies) whose defeat the benchmarks already predicted, then redesigning anyway

anti_rework_rules.rule: Capture the full recipe at the moment a result is kept
anti_rework_rules.prevents: unreproducible winners that force re-discovery of a working model/prompt/param combination the pipeline already paid to find

anti_rework_rules.rule: Register every fix (class -> fix -> recurrence check) in the regression log at fix time
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-diagnosing and re-fixing the same defect class next reel because the fix lived only in one session's memory

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify a swap target's media roles and duration support before swapping
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discovering after generation that veo3_1 takes no end frame for the seam, or that a 3 s slot silently clamped to 4 s and broke the beat grid

anti_rework_rules.rule: Apply the per-model trim preset before hero-grade matching on any new model's first batch
anti_rework_rules.prevents: regrading the whole reel when the new model's color signature surfaces at the timeline instead of at intake

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect survives 2-3 re-rolls of the same prompt/model
iteration_protocol.action: reclassify it systematic, close the re-roll lane for that class, and escalate through the dispatch table (prompt if addressable, else swap or redesign)

iteration_protocol.trigger: a shot's credit ceiling is reached
iteration_protocol.action: fire the mandatory trichotomy: accept under the compression rule if the residual qualifies, redesign the shot, or drop it and recut the reel

iteration_protocol.trigger: get_cost probes return real per-cell prices
iteration_protocol.action: re-denominate all ceilings in credits, recompute the reel envelope and exploration share, and retire every attempt-count prior

iteration_protocol.trigger: a previously fixed defect class recurs in QC
iteration_protocol.action: triage against the registry: restore a silently dropped fix (e.g. a lost prompt clause), or if the fix genuinely died, reopen the class into dispatch as new and update its registry row

iteration_protocol.trigger: the model catalog changes on re-enumeration
iteration_protocol.action: reopen regression classes whose fixes were model-relative, re-baseline the per-model failure ledger for changed models, and re-verify swap constraints (roles, durations, minima)

iteration_protocol.trigger: an A/B trial concludes with an attributable winner
iteration_protocol.action: log the full recipe, update the per-model ledger and the dispatch table's per-class defaults, and promote the winner as the seed recipe for its shot type

iteration_protocol.trigger: phone-screen QC contradicts the desktop verdict (a hidden cue shows, or a flagged cue vanishes)
iteration_protocol.action: recalibrate the acceptance lane's item boundaries against the observed compressed artifact and update the realism rubric's post-fix guidance

iteration_protocol.trigger: a shipped reel surfaces a tell the ship verdict missed
iteration_protocol.action: root-cause which gate or acceptance call failed, add the miss as a regression class with a recurrence check, and tighten the verdict's condition list

priority_rationale: The frame, gate order and credit preflight come first because every other unit assumes the loop shape, the fixed gate sequence and priced attempts; the four gates plus the critic boundary come next because they generate the failure signal everything downstream consumes; defect classification and the five levers precede dispatch because the table only routes what is classified into levers that exist; the budgets wrap dispatch in stop rules; the trial/log/regression trio turns spend into cumulative memory per the owner's keep-what-wins directive; and compression acceptance plus the ship verdict come last because they are the only places imperfection is legitimately accepted and the reel finally leaves the loop.
